desc:
You are given an array nums of non-negative integers and a list of queries. Query [left, right], when kept, may lower each element at positions left..right by at most 1, chosen independently for every element.

You may delete some queries. Return the maximum number of queries you can delete such that the remaining ones can still turn nums into all zeros (exactly zero). If even keeping all queries cannot do it, return -1.

nums = [2, 0, 2], queries = [[0, 2], [0, 2], [0, 0], [2, 2]]
result = 2

Positions 0 and 2 each need two covering queries; the first two queries cover both, so the last two can be deleted.
hints: Position i can become zero exactly when at least nums[i] of the kept queries cover it. So you want a smallest set of queries such that every position is covered enough times.
Sweep positions from left to right. When position i does not have enough active queries yet, you must pick more queries among those that start at or before i and have not ended before it.

Among the candidates, picking the one with the farthest right end is never worse (greedy). Use a max-heap of right ends for queries that have started, and a difference array to track how many chosen queries are active. If you run out of candidates (or the best one ends before i), the answer is -1.
editorial: Minimising kept queries is the same as maximising deletions. For one position the choice among covering queries only matters for the positions to its right, and a query with a farther right end covers a superset of the future positions of any query with a nearer end (all candidates already cover the current position). That makes the greedy 'pick the longest-reaching candidate' optimal by an exchange argument.

Implementation: sort queries by left end. Walk i from 0 to n - 1; push the right ends of queries with left = i onto a max-heap; maintain active = number of chosen queries covering i using a difference array (chosen query with end r adds +1 now and -1 at r + 1). While active < nums[i], pop the largest right end; if the heap is empty or that end is less than i return -1; otherwise choose it. At the end the answer is len(queries) - chosen.
Each query enters and leaves the heap once: O((n + q) log q) time, O(n + q) space.
solution:
import heapq


def maxRemovable(nums, queries):
    n = len(nums)
    starts = [[] for _ in range(n)]
    for left, right in queries:
        starts[left].append(right)
    heap = []
    expire = [0] * (n + 1)
    active = 0
    chosen = 0
    for i in range(n):
        active -= expire[i]
        for r in starts[i]:
            heapq.heappush(heap, -r)
        while active < nums[i]:
            if not heap or -heap[0] < i:
                return -1
            r = -heapq.heappop(heap)
            chosen += 1
            active += 1
            expire[r + 1] += 1
    return len(queries) - chosen
